walkthroughs.body_html:
Introduction to Economics — a core area of Economics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Introduction to Economics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Introduction to Economics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Ricardo published 'Principles of Political Economy and Taxation' in:

options: The value of the next-best alternative foregone when a choice is made — the real cost of a decision in terms of what you give up.
Opportunity cost is the money price of something.
Opportunity cost is the total of everything you give up when making a choice.
Real GDP is GDP only from physical goods; nominal GDP includes services.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between real GDP, nominal GDP and GNI?
options: Real GDP, nominal GDP and GNI are interchangeable terms.
Opportunity cost is the money price of something.

Nominal GDP uses current prices; real GDP adjusts for inflation; GNI (Gross National Income) is GDP plus net income from abroad (similar to old GNP). Each answers a different question about economic activity.
Real GDP is GDP only from physical goods; nominal GDP includes services.

mcqs.q: Why do economists generally argue against protectionism?
options: Protectionism means protecting national parks from development.
Protectionism always makes a country richer by keeping money at home.

Tariffs and quotas raise prices for consumers, protect inefficient industries, invite retaliation, and reduce overall welfare — even when they save specific jobs, the cost per job saved typically exceeds the wage.
Real GDP is GDP only from physical goods; nominal GDP includes services.
